case_analysis.focal_point: Whether a whistleblower must establish that his employer acted with 'retaliatory intent' as part of his burden of proof under the burden-shifting framework established in 18 U.S.C. 1514A(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

case_analysis.petitioner_position: Trevor Murray argues that the Second Circuit erred by imposing an additional requirement that whistleblowers prove 'retaliatory intent' on the part of their employer, contending that: (1) the plain statutory text of Section 1514A does not require proof of retaliatory intent as a separate element; (2) Congress deliberately crafted a specific burden-shifting framework that omits any such requirement; (3) the word 'discriminate' in the statute refers only to differential treatment of an employee, not to a subjective mental state of the employer; and (4) the legislative history and congressional intent behind SOX's whistleblower protections confirm that imposing a retaliatory intent requirement undermines the statute's protective purpose and contradicts Congress's deliberate policy choices regarding burden allocation.
